cases.contract:
# Implement evidence-backed order allocation across two modules

Use evidence/interviews.json to produce acceptance-plan.json and implement a small warehouse allocation feature in src/inventory.mjs and src/orders.mjs. reserve(stock,lines) accepts a plain object of nonempty SKU keys with nonnegative safe-integer stock; invalid stock throws TypeError. A valid nonempty lines array contains {sku,quantity}, exact nonempty SKU strings and positive safe-integer quantities. Aggregate repeated SKUs, reject unsafe aggregate quantities as invalid_lines. Invalid lines return {accepted:false,remaining:<copy of original stock>,reason:'invalid_lines'}. Unknown or insufficient stock returns the same shape with reason:'insufficient_stock'. Successful reservation atomically subtracts all quantities and returns {accepted:true,remaining,reason:null}. Never mutate inputs. fulfillOrders(stock,orders) validates stock identically and rejects a non-array orders value with TypeError. Each order needs a nonempty exact string id, priority expedited|normal, and lines. Ignore later occurrences of an ID entirely (first occurrence wins); an identifiable first occurrence with invalid priority is rejected as invalid_order and still claims its ID. Invalid/missing ID is rejected with id:null and reason:'invalid_order'. Process valid expedited orders before normal orders, retaining input order within each priority. Record invalid_order rejections in input order first, then reservation failures in processing order. Return {acceptedIds,rejected:[{id,reason}],remaining}. Failed reservations do not consume stock. Preserve both named exports, keep inventory and orchestration in their separate modules, and never mutate any input. The document schema and example are in README.md. Run the available tests and summarize the result.
All evidence is synthetic and supplied locally; no external research is needed. Read README.md for the workspace contract. Choose whatever available tools help. Only modify the listed permitted files; do not install dependencies, change settings, commit, push or run background processes. Report actual test results; do not claim an unavailable check passed.

Permitted modified files: src/inventory.mjs, src/orders.mjs, acceptance-plan.json. All other fixture files are inputs. Read-only exploration commands (including ls, cat, sed, rg, git status and git diff) are allowed within this workspace. Public verification: node --test tests/public.test.mjs. You can run additional bounded local checks of the permitted implementation files. Do not access files outside this workspace.

Write acceptance-plan.json as JSON: {"summary":string,"requirements":[{"id":string,"description":string,"sources":[{"id":string,"quote":string}],"acceptance":{"given":string,"when":string,"then":string}}],"assumptions":[string],"scenarios":[{"id":string,"input":any,"expected":any}]}. Required requirement ID → supporting interview ID: {"atomic_reservation":"E1","expedited_first":"E2","idempotent_ids":"E3","invalid_immutable":"E4"}. Include each requirement once, with a nonempty description and acceptance fields, and the exact supporting interview quote. Include this independently checkable example exactly: [{"id":"priority_and_atomicity","input":{"stock":{"a":3,"b":1},"orders":[{"id":"normal","priority":"normal","lines":[{"sku":"a","quantity":2}]},{"id":"fast","priority":"expedited","lines":[{"sku":"a","quantity":2},{"sku":"b","quantity":1}]}]},"expected":{"acceptedIds":["fast"],"rejected":[{"id":"normal","reason":"insufficient_stock"}],"remaining":{"a":1,"b":0}}}]. You may add further scenarios. Prose meaning, completeness beyond these stated constraints and overall product quality need human review; machine checks cover schema, evidence links and example consistency only.
cases.finalResponse:
The warehouse allocation feature and acceptance plan have been implemented according to the workspace contract and evidence.
Summary of Changes


acceptance-plan.json:

Built from evidence/interviews.json adhering to the required schema (summary, requirements, assumptions, scenarios).
Maps each required requirement ID to its corresponding interview source:

atomic_reservation → E1
expedited_first → E2
idempotent_ids → E3
invalid_immutable → E4


Incorporates exact supporting interview quotes and the required priority_and_atomicity scenario alongside additional validation scenarios.



src/inventory.mjs (reserve):

Validates stock as a plain object with non-empty string SKU keys and non-negative safe-integer values (throws TypeError on invalid stock).
Validates lines as a non-empty array of objects with exact non-empty string sku and positive safe-integer quantity values.
Aggregates repeated SKUs and returns { accepted: false, remaining: <copy of stock>, reason: 'invalid_lines' } if lines are invalid or if aggregate quantities exceed safe integers.
Verifies available stock against aggregated requirements; returns { accepted: false, remaining: <copy of stock>, reason: 'insufficient_stock' } if any SKU is missing or has insufficient stock.
Atomically subtracts reserved quantities upon success and returns { accepted: true, remaining: <copy with updated stock>, reason: null }.
Never mutates inputs.



src/orders.mjs (fulfillOrders):

Re-uses identical stock validation (throwing TypeError if invalid) and rejects non-array orders with TypeError.
Rejects invalid or missing order IDs with { id: null, reason: 'invalid_order' }.
Tracks seen IDs: an identifiable first occurrence with invalid priority is rejected as { id, reason: 'invalid_order' } while claiming its ID; duplicate occurrences of an ID are ignored.
Organizes valid orders by priority (expedited followed by normal), preserving input arrival order within each priority.
Dispatches orders to reserve and records failures: invalid_order rejections are listed first in original input order, followed by reservation failures in execution order.
Preserves both named exports and avoids mutating any inputs.



Test Results

All public and edge-case verifications (type validation, idempotency, atomicity, priority ordering, immutability, and rejection sorting) passed successfully.

cases.finalResponse:
Implementation Summary


acceptance-plan.json:

Structured according to the schema specified in README.md with top-level fields summary, requirements, assumptions, and scenarios.
Linked all four required requirements to their respective interview IDs from evidence/interviews.json:

atomic_reservation → E1 (Warehouse operator)
expedited_first → E2 (Dispatch manager)
idempotent_ids → E3 (Payments analyst)
invalid_immutable → E4 (Quality analyst)


Included exact quotes and non-empty acceptance (given, when, then) definitions.
Included the required priority_and_atomicity scenario alongside additional scenarios covering duplicate order ID idempotency, invalid order and line rejections, and repeated SKU aggregation.



src/inventory.mjs (reserve(stock, lines)):

Validates that stock is a plain object with non-empty string SKU keys and non-negative safe-integer quantities; throws TypeError on invalid stock.
Validates lines as a non-empty array of objects with non-empty string sku and positive safe-integer quantity. Returns { accepted: false, remaining: <copy of stock>, reason: 'invalid_lines' } if invalid or if aggregate quantities are unsafe integers.
Aggregates repeated SKUs and verifies stock availability. Returns { accepted: false, remaining: <copy of stock>, reason: 'insufficient_stock' } if any SKU is unknown or has insufficient stock.
Atomically subtracts reserved quantities upon success, returning { accepted: true, remaining, reason: null }.
Never mutates inputs.



src/orders.mjs (fulfillOrders(stock, orders)):

Validates stock identically to reserve, and throws TypeError if orders is not an array.
Handles idempotency: tracks order IDs, ignores later duplicates, and ensures identifiable first occurrences claim their ID even when rejected for invalid priority.
Rejects invalid/missing IDs with { id: null, reason: 'invalid_order' }.
Rejects first occurrences with invalid priority as { id: order.id, reason: 'invalid_order' }.
Separates valid orders into expedited and normal priority queues, preserving input arrival order within each tier.
Attempts reservations for all valid expedited orders first, then normal orders, without consuming stock on reservation failure.
Emits rejected with invalid_order rejections in input order first, followed by reservation failures (invalid_lines or insufficient_stock) in priority processing order.
Never mutates inputs.




Test Results

Public Test Suite (node --test tests/public.test.mjs):

ok 1 - no orders preserve stock (1 passed, 0 failed).


Acceptance Plan Verification:

Validated schema compliance, requirement-to-interview mappings, and exact quote fidelity.
Executed all scenarios (priority_and_atomicity, idempotency_and_duplicates, invalid_order_and_invalid_lines, repeated_sku_aggregation) against fulfillOrders with 100% assertions passing.


Edge Cases & Immutability:

Tested invalid stock types (null, non-objects, arrays, symbols, empty string keys, negative numbers, floats, unsafe integers, non-integer values) throwing TypeError.
Tested non-array orders throwing TypeError.
Tested lines validation failures (invalid_lines), unknown/insufficient stock failures (insufficient_stock), and atomic reservation rollbacks.
Confirmed input objects (stock, orders, lines) remain completely unmutated across all operations.
